scope: v2: recommendation consistency + tone + sample-vs-total + hedged-vs-asserted

findings.message: Priority 4 (Discovery Readiness 30/100) is listed in the Priorities section but the 'Critical Fixes' phase in What's Next covers only P1, P2, P3, and the 'Full Optimisation' phase lists P1–P6 — however the phase table's Scope column for Critical Fixes explicitly excludes P4, meaning P4 has no dedicated early-phase coverage and its first appearance in any phase label is only implicit within the P1–P6 catch-all, while the report's own narrative singles out Discovery Readiness as a high-priority cross-cutting item warranting earlier attention.
findings.context: | Critical Fixes | P1, P2, P3 (Compliance Risk) | Priority 1, 2, 3 resolved — WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility compliance restored |

findings.message: Priority 4 states that 'pages present on the server risk being underweighted or missed' and directs the client to confirm 'canonical declarations on any pages outside that set', but then asserts 'the Discovery Readiness score of 30/100 warrants confirming that coverage holds across the full sitemap' — treating the 30/100 score derived from 7 audited pages as if it characterises the full 485-URL sitemap.
findings.context: the Discovery Readiness score of 30/100 warrants confirming that coverage holds across the full sitemap

findings.message: The Structured Data Findings section states 'Organization entity has no name — entire entity is meaningless across the 5 audited pages where this gap was recorded', but the surrounding prose asserts 'WCAG AA issues across the audited set' and the structured-data table row presents this as a site-level pattern without scope qualification, implying the finding extends beyond the 5 pages on which it was actually observed.
findings.context: Organization entity has no name — entire entity is meaningless across the 5 audited pages where this gap was recorded

findings.message: The Findings priorities consistently use first-person voice ('We recorded', 'We find'), but the Optional Enhancements block immediately following the numbered priorities switches to impersonal third-person construction ('connecting each Person and Organization node', 'the two Book entries in the structured data inventory are natural candidates') without any first-person attribution, breaking the voice established across all six priority blocks.
findings.context: the two Book entries in the structured data inventory are natural candidates for aggregated review signals
